title: Leakage in customer churn features
prompt: A churn model predicts whether a customer cancels within 30 days. The training table has one row per customer snapshot and includes `refund_issued_at`, `cancellation_reason`, rolling usage, plan, and support contacts. Define the prediction timestamp and identify leakage risks, split strategy, and feature-generation checks.
expected_concepts: Features must be available at the prediction timestamp
Post-outcome fields are direct leakage
Rolling windows need strict historical cutoffs
Splits should prevent future or customer overlap as appropriate
Feature pipelines should enforce temporal joins

rubric.criterion: Defines prediction time and outcome window
Identifies direct and temporal leakage features
Chooses a defensible validation split
Proposes enforceable feature-timestamp checks

hints: Ask whether each value existed when the prediction would be made.
Snapshot construction must respect both entity and time boundaries.
follow_ups: How would delayed cancellation labels affect training data?
Which monitoring signal could reveal production feature leakage?

title: Metrics for rare fraud review
prompt: Fraud occurs in 0.5% of transactions and investigators can review only 200 alerts daily. Explain why accuracy is inadequate, select primary evaluation metrics for model comparison and threshold selection, and state how review capacity changes the decision rule.
expected_concepts: Class imbalance makes accuracy uninformative
Precision and recall expose different error costs
Precision-recall curves suit rare positive classes
Operational capacity imposes a threshold or top-k constraint

rubric.criterion: Explains the accuracy failure with imbalance
Chooses and interprets precision and recall metrics
Connects threshold selection to business costs
Incorporates the daily review limit

hints: A model predicting no fraud is almost perfectly accurate.
The team acts on a limited ranked set, not every positive score.
follow_ups: When would recall at a fixed precision be useful?
How would probability calibration help investigators?

title: Train validation and test roles
prompt: Explain the distinct roles of training, validation, and test sets in a supervised learning project. State where preprocessing is fitted, when the test set may be consulted, and what goes wrong if model choices repeatedly use test performance.
expected_concepts: Training data fits model parameters
Validation data supports model and threshold choices
Test data estimates final generalization once
Preprocessing must fit only on training partitions
Repeated test use leaks selection information

rubric.criterion: Distinguishes all three dataset roles
Places preprocessing fitting correctly
Restricts test evaluation appropriately
Explains selection bias from repeated test use

hints: Separate learning parameters from choosing among alternatives.
Treat the test set as unavailable until the pipeline is fixed.
follow_ups: How does cross-validation alter the validation role?
When is a temporal split preferable to a random split?

title: Diagnose linear regression assumptions
prompt: A linear regression predicts delivery time. Residuals curve upward with distance, spread grows with the fitted value, and neighboring deliveries from the same route have similar residuals. Interpret each pattern, state which goals are affected, and propose diagnostics or model changes without claiming that every violation invalidates prediction.
expected_concepts: Curvature suggests misspecified functional form
Growing spread indicates heteroscedasticity
Within-route similarity indicates dependent errors
Inference and prediction may be affected differently
Transformations, added structure, robust errors, or grouped models address different issues

rubric.criterion: Correctly interprets all three residual patterns
Separates inference consequences from predictive usefulness
Proposes issue-specific diagnostics
Proposes defensible model or uncertainty changes

hints: Map each visual pattern to one assumption rather than one universal fix.
Standard errors and point predictions do not fail in identical ways.
follow_ups: How would a route-level random effect help?
When might a tree model improve prediction but reduce interpretability?

title: Choose a grouped validation design
prompt: A medical dataset has several visits per patient, and the model will predict outcomes for entirely new patients. Compare ordinary random k-fold validation with grouped k-fold validation, choose one, and explain how preprocessing and class balance should be handled inside folds.
expected_concepts: Patient overlap leaks individual-specific information
Group-aware folds match the deployment unit
Preprocessing fits separately within each training fold
Stratification and grouping may require tradeoffs or specialized splitters

rubric.criterion: Identifies patient overlap as invalid validation
Chooses group-aware validation for the deployment goal
Places preprocessing within each fold
Addresses class-balance limitations honestly

hints: The independent unit is the patient, not the visit row.
Every learned transformation belongs inside the training side of a fold.
follow_ups: What changes when predicting future visits for known patients?
How would you create a final untouched test set?

title: Set a classifier threshold
prompt: A calibrated classifier estimates default probability. Missing a default costs about 20 times more than reviewing a safe applicant, but reviewers can process at most 8% of applications. Describe how to choose and validate a decision threshold, including which dataset is used and how uncertain cost assumptions are handled.
expected_concepts: Thresholds encode error costs and capacity constraints
Choose the threshold on validation data, not test data
Evaluate confusion outcomes and expected cost
Use sensitivity analysis for uncertain costs
Confirm calibration and final performance separately

rubric.criterion: Combines cost and review-capacity constraints
Uses validation data for threshold selection
Evaluates expected outcomes at candidate thresholds
Includes calibration and cost sensitivity checks
Reserves final test evaluation

hints: A probability of 0.5 has no special status under unequal costs.
Capacity may determine a score quantile before costs are optimized.
follow_ups: What if probabilities are poorly calibrated but ranking is strong?
How would policy fairness constraints enter threshold selection?

title: Control overfitting in boosted trees
prompt: Training loss for a gradient-boosted tree model keeps falling while validation loss begins rising after 300 rounds. Explain the pattern and prioritize changes involving learning rate, tree complexity, subsampling, regularization, and early stopping. State how these choices interact.
expected_concepts: Diverging validation loss indicates overfitting
Early stopping selects rounds using validation performance
Learning rate trades off with number of trees
Depth and leaf constraints control weak-learner complexity
Subsampling and regularization reduce variance

rubric.criterion: Diagnoses overfitting from the loss curves
Uses early stopping without test leakage
Explains learning-rate and round interaction
Proposes justified complexity and regularization changes
Avoids changing every parameter without validation

hints: The best number of rounds is not necessarily the largest trained number.
Smaller steps usually require more boosting rounds.
follow_ups: How would noisy validation loss affect early stopping patience?
Why can very deep base trees undermine boosting?

title: Cluster stores with mixed scales
prompt: You must cluster stores using annual revenue, floor area, return rate, and latitude/longitude. Explain preprocessing, distance assumptions, how to assess candidate k values, and why apparently stable clusters may still be operationally meaningless. Address outliers and geographic coordinates.
expected_concepts: K-means depends on Euclidean scale and roughly spherical clusters
Standardization prevents large-unit features from dominating
Raw latitude and longitude need context-appropriate distance treatment
Outliers can pull centroids
Internal metrics require stability and domain validation

rubric.criterion: Explains scale and distance assumptions
Handles geographic features and outliers thoughtfully
Uses multiple diagnostics for selecting k
Requires operational interpretation and stability checks

hints: Revenue units should not silently dominate every distance.
A high silhouette score does not establish business usefulness.
follow_ups: When would DBSCAN be a better candidate?
How would you test cluster stability across samples?
